segments.title: Clear keeps your place
segments.body: ↓ Clear sweeps the tabs and leaves the one you're reading. It used to take that one too.

segments.title: New tabs move in next door
segments.body: With Settings › Tabs › Below the current tab, ⌘T opens right under where you are. Before, only top or bottom.

segments.title: Pinned splits stay split
segments.body: Close one pane and the pinned split stays one row. It used to fall apart into two.

segments.title: Middle-click twice
segments.body: The first middle-click closes a pinned tab, the second removes it, with Undo in case you didn't mean it.

segments.title: No Icon
segments.body: A group can wear Dia's neutral stack instead of borrowing its first tab's favicon.

segments.title: Dots that say who
segments.body: Hover a profile dot and its name floats above it, the way Dia does it.
segments.afterOnly: A plain macOS tooltip. macOS only draws it for a real pointer, so a hidden test instance can't film it.

segments.title: ⌥⇧-click opens a split
segments.body: A link opens beside the page instead of in a whole new window. Settings › Tabs can make it plain ⌥-click.

segments.title: Screens bring their sound
segments.body: Sharing a screen or a window can include its audio now. Before, only tabs could.
